svg.title: kG: volts to hold up against gravity
svg.desc: Animated, two parts. Left, an elevator carriage moves up and down between rails and holds at three heights; a green arrow pushes it up and a dark arrow, gravity, pulls it down, and its green volts bar stays the same at every height: kG. Right, an arm on a motor swings from level up to 45 degrees and to straight up, and back; gravity always pulls its end straight down. Its volts bar is kG times cos(angle): full when the arm is level, smaller as it rises, and empty when it points straight up. Level, all of the weight hangs on the motor; straight up, none does. REV calls the arm's version kCos.
svg.text: kG: volts to hold up against gravity
An elevator's is the same everywhere; an arm's is kG × cos(angle).
Level, all of the arm's weight hangs on the motor; straight up, none does.
REV calls the arm's version kCos. Use kG or kCos, never both.
